opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time, Kofi. I'm a researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group that studies how people see changes at work, and nothing you tell me will be linked to your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Yeah, cool. I don't really know much about this stuff, but go for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Picture this. AI stays a handy tool, like a better search engine. Hiring, pay and prices carry on the way they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's a thing on your phone. I use it sometimes to ask stuff. Not a big deal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For me nothing changes. I'm still trying to get good on the forwarder. That's my real problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep putting in hours on the machine. Watch some videos on the controls, because I keep messing up the crane.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fine. Bit stressed about the controls, but that's not AI.

S0.say: It's a thing on your phone. I use it to ask stuff sometimes. Not a big deal.
S0.think: Nothing changes. My real problem is getting good on the forwarder.
S0.do: Puts in hours on the machine and watches videos to get better with the crane controls.
S0.feel: Fine. A bit stressed about the controls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now picture this. Very capable AI exists, but it spreads slowly, over ten years or more. Some tasks disappear, but few whole jobs do. Companies hire fewer beginners. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say that sucks for people my age. Everyone says get a start somewhere, but if nobody hires beginners, how do you start?

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm a beginner, and not the best one. If they keep fewer of us, they keep the good ones. That's not me right now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Try harder, I guess. Ask the senior guy for more seat time. See if there's a course the company or the government would pay for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Kind of uneasy. Like getting picked last.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a course yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nah. I don't have the money. If it's free, I'm there.

S1.say: If nobody hires beginners, how are people my age supposed to start?
S1.think: I'm a beginner and not the best one. If they keep fewer of us, it won't be me.
S1.do: Asks the senior operator for more seat time and looks for a course someone else will pay for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Next one. Within 5 years, AI assistants that can act on their own handle most routine office work. There are layoffs and pay pressure in office jobs. Some new AI-related jobs appear, and politicians argue loudly about what to do. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Good thing I don't work in an office. I'd probably make a joke about it with my mates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That's not really my world. But if new AI jobs show up, maybe there's one that suits me better than this machine. I don't know.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Find out what those new jobs even are. If there's free training, I'd sign up. Otherwise keep doing what I'm doing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Okay. Kind of curious, actually.

S2.say: Good thing I don't work in an office.
S2.think: That's not my world. But maybe one of the new AI jobs would suit me better than this machine.
S2.do: Looks into what the new AI jobs are and signs up for any free training.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now a faster version. Within 2 to 3 years, AI matches skilled professionals at most thinking work. Lots of office and professional workers lose their jobs. Share and house prices boom. There's a political crisis over who should get the gains. Physical jobs are mostly untouched. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say finally the guys in suits get it. Everyone looked down on jobs like mine, and now we're the safe ones.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. If office people lose their jobs, some of them come out here wanting work. Some of them would learn the machine faster than me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Stop messing around and actually practise. Save a bit, since I live with my parents and don't pay much.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Half good, half nervous.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does 'actually practise' look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Getting in early. Asking for feedback instead of hiding when I mess up. Stuff I should be doing anyway.

S3.say: Finally the guys in suits get it. Now jobs like mine are the safe ones.
S3.think: Office people might come out here wanting work, and some would learn the machine faster than me.
S3.do: Gets in early, asks for feedback, practises on the machine, and saves while living with his parents.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Last one. Everything in the previous picture happens, and on top of that, general-purpose robots arrive in warehouses, kitchens, building sites, farms and care homes within 3 to 5 years. Hands-on work is no longer a safe place to be. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say that's messed up. They need to look after people like me, not just the companies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That's me done. I already struggle with the controls. A machine that drives itself in the forest doesn't need a guy who's bad at driving it. And there's nothing else around here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Leave, probably. Go to a city, find whatever training is going and get the government to pay for it. Find somewhere cheap to stay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Bad. Like the floor's going. Glad I'm still at my parents' place, honestly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said there's nothing else around here. Would you really leave?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the work's gone, yeah. I'm young. It's my parents I'd worry about leaving.

S4.say: That's messed up. They need to look after people like me, not just the companies.
S4.think: That's me done. A machine that drives itself doesn't need a guy who's bad at driving it.
S4.do: Plans to move to a city, find any training going and get the government to pay for it.
S4.feel: Like the floor's going. Glad to still live at home.
